title: Test: The Nervous System
summary: Check what you learned across the whole chapter.

questions.q: The section **Real-Time Command Transport and Bus Determinism** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Sample-and-hold, compute, and bus transport each subtract omega_c*tau of phase at crossover, so fast loops must close inside the drive and the permission tick can supervise them but never sit in them.

Authority over an admitted chunk ends at the earliest of four independent events (evidence freshness deadline, lease expiry, host heartbeat timeout, protective reflex), and a heartbeat proves only that the host is alive, never that its motion is valid.

The permission path must be the sole writer of every electrical path that can energize a winding, because one unmediated write puts proposer and drives in one failure domain, and the stop itself must be specified in hardware.
A declared WCET is an analytical upper bound on a task's run time on a given processor, distinct from the unknown true worst case and from any measured maximum.

questions.q: Which statement captures **Rate tiers from time constants**?
options: Proposals cross rate boundaries as state messages, not events, so a single-slot seqlock or wait-free multi-slot mailbox gives the faster reader one bounded, nonblocking attempt per tick that returns a complete snapshot or keeps the previous one.

Each tier takes its rate from a different physical constant (winding L/R and the PWM carrier for the current loop, base travel per tick for the permission tick, weight-sweep cost for the chunk policy, prefill cost for the intent model), not from convenience.

An admitted chunk may drive the actuators only for a lease counted on the permission path's own clock, derived from the plant: longer than the renewal period plus jitter and short enough to fit under the pre-brake ceiling of the stopping budget.
